player.speaker: Revolutionary Delegate
line.artelt-cold-open.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-cold-open.text: Leave that order open. The stokers want to see the seal. Berlin is asking for an armistice, and the Admiralty still wants us out against the British. Who is going to tell the crews to sail?
line.artelt-opening.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-opening.text: They wouldn't sail on Thüringen or Helgoland. So the squadrons were sent back, and forty-seven men were arrested on the way to Kiel, most of them from Markgraf. Here are the names. We had two hundred and fifty sailors at the Union House last night. Souchon wouldn't even see our delegation.
line.garbe-union-house.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-union-house.text: You won't get into the hall again. The police have chained it shut. There are five hundred sailors outside; we've sent them to the Großer Exerzierplatz. The presses are running for tomorrow. They want peace and bread, Karl, as well as the prisoners.
line.popp-socialists.speaker: Lothar Popp
line.popp-socialists.text: Then let the yards hear that the meeting is still on. I need the station and telegraph before Souchon sends his own account. He'll call this a mutiny by a few ships if we let him.
line.artelt-confronts-popp.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-confronts-popp.text: Those forty-seven got the crews out here, Lothar. What do I tell their shipmates? Wait at the gate while we send a telegram?
line.garbe-steinhaeuser.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-steinhaeuser.text: Another runner from Feldstraße. Lieutenant Steinhäuser has formed thirty recruits across the road to the prison. Rifles loaded. He says the march stops there.
line.popp-coordination.speaker: Lothar Popp
line.popp-coordination.text: The hall chose you to coordinate the columns, Delegate. Karl has the torpedo crews; I have to bring out the yards. We can try the service gate now, or take the station, telegraph and armouries before Souchon cuts us off. I need to know where to send the men.
line.popp-coordination.choice.free-priso: The prison. Take a small party through the service gate now; the main column follows before Steinhäuser can turn the road into a firing line.
Gain an experienced half-strength sailor detachment and +50 prestige; the remaining escapees appear exposed inside the compound and must be reached before the guards break them up.
line.popp-coordination.choice.secure-com: Coordinate the city first. Put runners on the station, telegraph and armouries, then hold the rescue column ready for the prison.
Gain +140 prestige and +15 experience for every core formation; no prisoners appear at setup, but approaching the compound starts the rescue crisis and gives you one turn to break through.
line.popp-prisoners-objection.speaker: Lothar Popp
line.popp-prisoners-objection.text: I'll keep the presses going with whoever you leave me. Send a runner if the wires go. I need news from the prison before the barracks get Souchon's version.
line.garbe-prisoners.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-prisoners.text: The service gate is open—the first men are out and asking for rifles. The rest are caught in the inner yard; the alarm is hammering through the base. Steinhäuser's men are turning towards them. Reach the compound before the guards break the escape apart.
line.artelt-communications-objection.tex: All right, the rescue column waits. But keep it ready. When your runners get back, I want to move on Feldstraße. Don't send those men off on another errand.
line.garbe-communications.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-communications.text: The districts have their orders. Each section is checking its rifles and route. The prisoners are still inside. Bring the rescue column toward the compound and the crowd will follow. Steinhäuser has his men across that road; be ready for them to fire.
line.souchon-warning.speaker: Governor Souchon's Headquarters
line.souchon-warning.text: Order from Naval Governor Souchon: the Union House is closed. Disperse all unauthorised assemblies. Lieutenant Steinhäuser's patrol will block the march to the Feldstraße detention compound. Loyal detachments are to secure the station, telegraph and military depots. Ringleaders will be arrested before the morning watch.
line.artelt-final.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-final.text: So he means to arrest us too. Get the sailors and yard columns moving together. Disarm anyone who tries to stop them; let the soldiers who join keep their rifles. And send word to the ships: nobody sails.
